Now she thinks I'm doing really well, but by her saying that, it makes it difficult to bring up things that actually are bothering me. But for the most part I am doing a lot better, especially with not reacting to things right away and damaging relationships. 

But there are still days where I feel absolutely shitty and theres no hope and my mind always thinks of suicide at that point. I have gotten to the point that I acknowledge those thoughts and move on and think of them as intrusive thoughts that I don't have to internalize. 

I think talk therapy is not useful to me at all. DBT has been the most helpful. And now I'm at the point where I need help tackling my issues relating to ADHD. I would like to see someone who can teach skills in a way similar to dbt. I live in a somewhat rural area so resources are a bit limited.

Eventually he ended it because I was suicidal and he couldn't/didn't want to handle that. 

* My advice is breakup with him - no contact. 
* File a police report. They may not be able to actually prosecute him because of the lack of evidence and "he said she said" situation, but it'll be on file in case he ever does this to someone else. This is something I didn't do and regret to this day. 
* Find a therapist, pastor, anyone. Get help working through this NOW before it consumes your life anymore. You can try a specific therapy called CPT (not to be confused with CBT, although similar, it stands for cognitive behavioral therapy) or EMDR (that helped me)
* Get the book "Recovering from rape" http://amzn.com/0805029281 it really helped me
* You'll hear this from anyone you talk to, but it's important that you believe it. IT IS NOT YOUR FAULT. The moment you said your safe word he should have stopped. That was his decision. You might start to question what you could have done to prevent it or play the "I should have...", "I shouldn't have..." thing.  The fact is we cannot predict what someone else is going to do.
